parts.label: The big question
parts.title: Which holds more, 2 gal 1 qt or 10 qt? How can you be sure?
parts.body: Two units in one amount. Notice, wonder, then try it your way.

think.script:
Welcome to Hilltop Dairy!

[ON SCREEN: Dairy board]

Last night the Smudge knocked over the Gallon-Man, the statue at Farmer Hank's dairy. The board right under me has six dairy jobs. Each one puts a piece of him back.

[ON SCREEN: Two cans]

Here's the first puzzle. Hank has two milk cans. Can A holds 2 gallons 1 quart. Can B holds 10 quarts. Which can holds more milk, and by how many quarts?

[ON SCREEN: The big question]

First, climb the ladder on your page, so you know how many of each size fill the next one. Then, at the milk can puzzle, look at the two cans before you pour a drop. What do you notice? What do you wonder? Write that down, then try it your own way. Make a guess and hold on to it. On the Learn tab, the Math Crew will show you two ways. See if one matches yours.

learn.label: Learn · two ways, then fill the cream bottles
learn.title: Two Ways
learn.script:
Look at the two cans one more time. One has gallons and quarts. One has only quarts. We can't compare them until they're written the same way.

[ON SCREEN: Board: The cans]

[DRAW: point to Can A's row, 2 | 1. Write 10 qt beside the empty row for Can B.]

Can A, 2 gallons 1 quart. Can B, 10 quarts.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Two ways]

[DRAW: fill in Atlas's blanks as you say them, then Felix's.]

Atlas goes up the ladder. He pours Can B into gallon jugs. 4 quarts fill a jug, so 8 quarts fill 2 jugs, and 2 are left. 2 gallons 2 quarts. Felix goes down the ladder. 2 gallons is 2 times 4, 8 quarts, plus 1 is 9. 10 minus 9 is 1. Both ways say Can B, by 1 quart.

Pause here. Say out loud which way is more like what you did.

[ON SCREEN: Live: Fill the Cream Bottles]

[DO: tap each of the 3 quart bottles. Type 6 in the box and tap Check. Tap Next. Tap the 6 pint bottles one at a time.]

Hank's cream, 3 quarts. Each quart pours into 2 pints: 6 pints. Each pint into 2 cups: 12 cups. Going down, multiply. Going up, group. Now fill the cream bottles on your page.

do.label: Do · watch me solve (boards)
do.title: Watch Me Solve It
do.script:
Now watch me solve three. Pause any time.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 1]

[DRAW: write 3 × 2 = 6 under c. Then 6 × 8 = 48 under fl oz.]

3 pints, down to cups. Each pint is 2 cups, so 3 times 2 is 6 cups. Down one more step: each cup is 8 fluid ounces, so 6 times 8 is 48 fluid ounces.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 2]

Your turn first. Pause the video and try this one on paper. Then press play and check.

[DRAW: write 16 and 3 in the bond. Under 16 write 4 gal. Then 19 ÷ 4 gives 4 R 3, so 4 gal 3 qt.]

19 quarts, up to gallons. I group by 4: 16 quarts fill 4 gallons, and 3 quarts are left. Or 19 divided by 4 is 4, remainder 3. 4 gallons 3 quarts.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Problem 3]

[DRAW: under 10 gal write 10 × 4 = 40 qt. Then + 3 qt = 43 qt.]

10 gallons 3 quarts, all in quarts. 10 times 4 is 40, plus 3 is 43 quarts.

[ON SCREEN: Board: Spot the mistake]

[DRAW: circle 48 pt. Write going up: group by 2. 24 ÷ 2 = 12 pt.]

Is this right? Someone multiplied going up the ladder. Pints are bigger than cups, so there are fewer of them. Group by 2: 12 pints. Ask yourself every time: up or down?

wrap.title: The Gallon-Man Stands

parts.label: Two ways
parts.title: Down: multiply · Up: group
parts.body: One step at a time, with that step's number.

wrap.script:
Look how far you came!

[ON SCREEN: Two ways]

Today you climbed the capacity ladder, from fluid ounces all the way up to gallons. Going down the ladder, you multiply. Going up, you group, and a leftover stays in the smaller unit. And the milk cans? Can B holds more, by 1 quart.

[ON SCREEN: The plaque]

And the Smudge's plaque? You poured 5 quarts into a new gallon jug. 4 quarts filled it, and 1 was left. 3 gallons 5 quarts is really 4 gallons 1 quart.

[ON SCREEN: Next time]

The Gallon-Man stands again. Next time we climb the Clock Tower and work with hours, minutes and seconds. See you there, explorers!
